quest.title: Narration Footnotes
quest.description: Kirara says there are a few things she must investigate alone. As you're not a cat, curiosity won't kill you, so why not go with her...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're all good!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Great! Then let's go!

talks.objective: Follow Kirara to the village ahead

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Huh? I was sure there'd be people here...
...There once was a goddess who ruled over fate. Before she died, she left three riddles for the kingdom she'd created.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What... Who said that?
Long story short, on this day, a sentient feline, an outlander, and a, uh... diminutive pixie arrived on the scene.
They saw a narrow path off to the side.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, but which side?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Yeah, if you gave ambiguous instructions like that to a Komaniya Express courier, they'd give you the parcel right back and tell you to write the delivery address more clearly.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: ...Despite how obvious the answer was, the perplexed pixie and the flummoxed feline struggled to work it out. Hmm, although perhaps a small part of the blame could be attributed to my dull narration...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Alright, let's try this again: *clears throat* "The path on the left-hand side seemed to give off an enticing fragrance, as if to say: 'This is the way to wealth and glory!'"

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ooh! That sounds like the start of a good story! Then what, then what?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Police, open up!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: ...That's actually quite an amusing approach. It's probably not going to get us anywhere, but I do admire your sense of humor, and your commitment to it.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 1: Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're here for a routine inventory check.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Ah, what an ingenious idea! Far more intelligent than Boborano's ancestors. But I still recommend against this answer.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 1: Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Stop the poem, we have a situation... Something's up with this person.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Turns out... there's glue...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You try to stand up, but the glue is holding you firmly in place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, you can do it! Th—This can't be how our story ends...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Try to stand up)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You manage to partially un-stick yourself. The issue isn't that you can't break free — it's more that you don't want to tear your clothes in the process. They mean a lot to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Can I give you a hand? Or a tail, even?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Keep trying to stand up)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You finally free yourself and stand up, clothes intact.

talks.objective: Pull out the great clockwork key

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}-Marquis and {M#his}{F#her} retinue.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: The Great Youkai, Nekomata-in-Boots!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the Trusty Travel-Guide Pixie— Uhh, travel-guide! Trusty travel-guide.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 2: By which virtue did the ancients defeat the dragon?

talks.objective: Speak with the three within the Future Marquis' Abode-to-Be

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Is it just my imagination, or...?

talks.objective: Speak with the three within the Future Marquis' Abode-to-Be

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Ah, welcome, esteemed and noble outlander. Allow us to introduce ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: We represent the three great clans of this realm, having been selected as its authorized historical supervisors.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Our purpose being to await the arrival of ones such as yourselves, who shall remove the clockwork key.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: My name is—

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: You're Cappet, he's Albizzi, and that's Boborano. Right?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: You've done so much talking that we can already tell you apart by your voices.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aren't we missing someone, though? The guy who led us here to begin with?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Who?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: *clears throat* And thus was born the long-awaited fellowship, destined to uncover the truth of the past. Allow me to quote, if I may: "In the history of Constellation Metropole, a new page has begun."

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Him.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Well, there's no fourth person, so which of you is the ventriloquist? Come on, out with it.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: We've never heard that voice before. But he sounds like he'd be good at reading bedtime stories to children.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Whoever it is, I don't know and I don't care. Forget about him. We have far more important things to focus on, like where our journey goes from here.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: That key you hold is the pivot point about which the past and present of the Metropole revolve. However, between our three clans there is some... dispute over the historical record.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Each clan has its own version of history, detailing the clan's origins and the tale of the dragon of old. And unfortunately, we don't know which one is the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dragon? You mean, the one that's been acting up recently?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Oh — no, not that one, you adorable little pixie. When I say "dragon of old"—

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: ...He means, a dragon that would be really, really old if it was still with us today, but it was defeated in ancient times. The new one has nothing to do with our clan history.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Uhh, was that supposed to be a joke...? Anyway, so you've been waiting for someone to remove the key so you can finally explore the truth of the past?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Not just explore it, but argue incessantly about it. Honestly, I don't care that much. Cappet's the one who's always bothering us about it.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: What we need to figure out is who resolved the dragon crisis. We have to know that before we can decide which is the Supreme Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: The moment you removed the key from where it was lodged, you became the Honorary Marquis. We humbly beseech you, noble outlander—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Call me {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: #Noble Marquis {NICKNAME}, we ask you to help us — you, and your talking puss-in-boots, and the pale, floating pixie.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Puss-in-boots, are you serious!? It's better than "demon-feline," but still...

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Embrace it, my friend, embrace it. Most cats don't wear boots or speak, do they?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I'm not even a "cat"! I'm a nekomata! Now that you know the word, I expect you to use it!

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Please allow me to lead you all to a sacred memorial site. It will be much easier to explain what needs to be done once we are there.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cappet leads the party to the so-called "sacred memorial site."

talks.objective: Go to the sacred site of the Cappet clan

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: This place is sacred to my clan. It is where our brave forefathers once took up arms against the dragon of old.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: After a bitter battle that dragged on for many days and nights, finally our forefathers fought the dragon into submission, and it fled. ...They took turns, though. Some forefathers worked the day shift, while others worked the night shift.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So they worked shifts while the poor dragon had to work around the clock?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: So they say. It's just a legend though.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Wait a second! Did I just hear you admit that your clan's history is just a legend?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: History, legend — who cares? My clan was definitely courageous, that's the point. That's the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: And isn't the truth what we've all been arguing about non-stop for all these years?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #Cappet's words gave {NICKNAME} food for thought: Could it be that "the truth" in a fictional world is equivalent to "fiction" in the real world?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: But that would have to wait. Apparently, Cappet was not alone in his pilgrimage to this sacred site — unwanted company had arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and the talking cat— Ahem, nekomata decided to teach them some manners.

talks.objective: Defeat the opponent(s) standing before you

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Courage and strength.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Oh, no no no, don't say that. Even though the writings you saw do prove that bravery has its uses...

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Uh, you do realize we can hear everything you're saying, right?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: If you say it out loud, you'll only set those three off arguing again. Thinking it is fine, but please promise me you won't say it.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 2: By which virtue did the ancients defeat the dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Your martial prowess and show of courage are a more vivid re-enactment of my ancestors' feats that suit the modern aesthetic.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Now, let's get down to business.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: As we all know, time is but an illusion. Time may flow line-by-line, page-by-page, or frame-by-frame. But usually, it flows in the form of springs and gears.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: And that clockwork key you have in your hand can turn back time, and make the past reappear.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Actually, my view is that the illusion of time is more of a problem of consciousness. Gears power the body, while the body is the vessel of the conscious mind.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: But the mind cannot understand the dimension of time, so we experience instead an endless continuum of moments as the pinion of now turns along the rack of ages.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I... I'm getting flashbacks to when I was delivering packages to the Sumeru Akademiya...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: A teacher once asked Albizzi what his greatest fear was, and he replied: "dragons." Boborano was asked the same question. He replied "time," and repeated the argument we just heard.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The teacher then turned to Cappet, and posed the same question. He replied "Boborano."

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: The manuscript that tells the truth of the historical record, the blueprint to all of creation, the work of the great mage themselves — it can be found at the beginning of the gear-rack, and on the very first page of the book.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon didn't follow all that. But basically, you're just saying that we need to put the key in and turn it all the way back?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Exactly. It is said that in the beginning, the Goddess of Creation took the Goddess of Fate's manuscript as a blueprint, placed it under the Goddess of Prophecy's starry realm, and generated the world from a few magic arrays.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: So in a few moments, when the great clockwork key turns the local time here back to the very beginning, we will restore the magic arrays back to their original configurations.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Hold on, isn't stealing part of the blueprint of creation a little dangerous? Also, how are we supposed to know the original configurations of the magic arrays?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Ah, well the general shapes of the configurations have been passed down over the ages. They now form the family crests of each of our clans. So you'll just need to reference my family crest, and join the dots accordingly.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: To address your other concern... When the house has already been built, do you really think that taking away the construction crew and blueprint will cause it to collapse?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}-Marquis prepares to insert the great clockwork key into the nearby keyhole.

talks.objective: Complete the Oracle Pillar's picture (Open it to view hints)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hard work and wealth.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: ...To be completely honest, "hardwork" is a bit of an alien concept to us here in the Constellation Metropole. We have "hardware," and we have "clockwork," but not "hardwork."

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 2: By which virtue did the ancients defeat the dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Shop Owner
dialogues.text: Now recruiting miners!

talks.objective: Read the true history of the clan of "Valor"

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Behold, the sacred writings that record the truth of— No wait, that have shaped the truth of history. Gather around, and let us bear witness!

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Feast your eyes, rejoice, and cheer. For this is the unquestionable truth! Look at the signature — nobody is capable of forging that!

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: I don't believe it! So... all along, our histories have been false?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Don't lose heart, Albizzi. It does not follow from "his is true" that "ours are false."

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: That might be the most bogus logic I've ever heard! But keep up the mental gymnastics, Boborano. I've been waiting for that look of jealousy on your face my whole life, and I'm gonna savor it.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And yet, it seemed that this conundrum could indeed have more than one solution. Everyone agreed that there may be more than one truth.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The party decided to visit the sacred sites of the other clans, and see what their documents had to say.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Isn't a narrator supposed to remain detached and objective? It feels like you're forcing a narrative agenda on us here.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Well, whatever. I'm in a good mood, let's do it. The instructions say to repeat the process three times, and besides — I'm looking forward to watching you both be sorely disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Let's do my clan next. I'll lead the way.

talks.objective: Go to the sacred site of the Boborano clan

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps... both are equally real.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Hear, hear. Who can be sure that the outside world isn't just a dream? And that when the dreamer wakes up, they won't just find themselves inside a novel?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: There is no way to know, therefore both are equally real.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: All correct. You may have the key pedestal.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The door opens, and a puff of smoke wafts out.\nAfter the smoke clears, the pedestal appears.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}-Marquis, you know what must be done. Please insert the great clockwork key.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Oh — and this is my family crest.

talks.objective: Complete the Oracle Pillar's picture (Open it to view hints)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: If this is the right answer, I swear I'll—

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Ugh, a barefaced lie! So low.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 3: Which is more real, the fiction of the outside world, or the truth of this world?

dialogues.speaker: Grocery Store Owner
dialogues.text: We're closed, we're closed.

talks.objective: Read the true history of the clan of "Wisdom"

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Now, let me see what—

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: What elaborate fiction the clan of wisdom was able to conjure up.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: If anyone's listening, I would like to submit these as my last words: "I surrender. I'm the one who murdered Cappet."

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Haha, look! Look, my clan's history is true as well. There's that same unforgeable signature again, right here!

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Does this mean that my clan is the only odd one out...?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Given that my clan's wisdom is such a subject of ridicule in your eyes, I will now appeal to my own personal intelligence — which I believe far surpasses that of my clan at large — and make a prediction:

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: It seems likely that the claims made by each of our clans regarding their history and virtue are all true.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Boborano... How can that be?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ah, I get what's going on. Once when I was drinking with Guuji Yae, she bet me a round of Dried Fish that I couldn't guess which cup the Umeboshi was under.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Whichever one I guessed, I was always wrong, and Guuji Yae would lift a different cup to reveal the Umeboshi.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: But then I learned later from one of the shrine maidens, Miyuki, that all of the cups had an Umeboshi under them! *sigh*... Just goes to show, I still got a long way to go before I become a great youkai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't mind fox lady, that's just her way of teasing you!

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Oh! Actually, that reminds me. We can now open these three treasure chests. And unlike the guessing game you mentioned, this one's not a trick...

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Cool... Well, once you've plundered the last of Boborano's family wealth, we can go to my clan's place.

talks.objective: Go to the sacred site of the Albizzi clan

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The cohort of truth-seekers followed Albizzi to his clan's sacred site. They arrived to the sight of a giant guard towering over them.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Up ahead is my clan's gigantified guard. He can be a little pig-headed, and he's incredibly strong. Your weapons won't even scratch him.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Wait, but wasn't Cappet's clan the one that's all about strength? So... What do you guys believe in then?

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Oh, the guard is one of Cappet's people. Size is a coveted trait in the clan of strength, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Mine is the clan of empathy, and our key contribution is... growth serum!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: ...What's empathetic about that?

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Our ancestors believed that, just maybe, the dragon of old didn't mean us any harm at all. Perhaps the dragon simply didn't notice us, since we are so very tiny.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: So they drank the growth serum, and grew even larger than the dragon. Then, they sat the dragon down, calmly explained their perspective, and eventually taught it how to empathize.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Uhhh...

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: The serum isn't what it once was, though. Nowadays, it doesn't make you grow all that much, and it actually makes you lose your empathy... So, I advise we take a detour.

talks.objective: Go to the sacred site of the Albizzi clan
Find the base of the great clockwork key

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #C'mon, you'll have to do better than that, kid. I mean, {NICKNAME}-Marquis. You and your friends are the only ones who know the truth about us.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 3: Which is more real, the fiction of the outside world, or the truth of this world?

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: We should be getting close.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Why is this place so full of junk? Are you the kind of people who never throw away the box when you buy something, 'cause you're worried you won't be able to return it without the original packaging?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: We'll never find the Oracle Pillars in all this mess!

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Never mind that, we have a more pressing issue... It seems there's a slight problem with my clan's family crest. The Marquis may need to utilize their wisdom to solve the issue.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Wisdom too, huh? Well, you guys have a bit of everything, don't you? Except empathy.

talks.objective: Complete the Oracle Pillar's picture (Open it to view hints)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Both are false.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Please try to avoid being unnecessarily cruel in your response.

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 3: Which is more real, the fiction of the outside world, or the truth of this world?

talks.objective: Return to the base of the great clockwork key
Read the true history of the clan of "Empathy"

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: This is the last one.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: The signature! ...So it's true! Empathy is one of the founding virtues of Constellation Metropole too!

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Just as we suspected. All three are the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Okay, well this is a lot to process. I feel a little empty inside... Yes, we found the truth, but... there's too much truth.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I get you. It's like... in Inazuma, when there were only six books in the Mirage Warriors series, it was really popular.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: But by the time book number eighty-eight came out, nobody wanted to read it. They'd all lost interest.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: A brief moment of joy is drowned out by a growing feeling of melancholy. But perhaps there is a glimmer of hope to be found, too?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Anyone? Anyone? Alright, I'll say it: How is it the case that these three versions of history can all be true at once?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's exactly what Paimon was wondering... But Boborano kind of already explained it away earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Paimon was worried she'd look stupid for asking the question.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: It's not a stupid question at all, my dear little pixie. While I did postulate that different truths may coexist, there is an issue when it comes to these three truths in particular.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: The problem is, all three truths are the history of the exact same thing — namely, the dragon and the Metropole's origins. Yet all three bear the signature, showing that they're genuine.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Suddenly, the sound of a bell rings out!

talks.objective: Escape from the clan of "Empathy"'s sacred site

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Phew, we made it out. Dunno if we'll still be needing this clockwork key, but I yoinked it out before we ran, just in case!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, but back to the truth problem. There are three conflicting versions of the truth, and somehow they're all still true. What is that supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: I don't know. I doubt anyone here in Simulanka could make sense of it. All we do know is that any manuscript bearing her signature has to be valid.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: She is the Goddess of Fate, the creator of all of this. And all these manuscripts are her grand design.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: The reason we argued about who was right was that we didn't know enough about the truth of the past. But now we have the truth, so we just have to accept it.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: As surely as we will follow the clockwork path designed for us, so is this the course that history has taken. It is clear and incontrovertible.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: We will never argue again. Thank you all.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Is that all there is to it? Is this where the decision made at the first crossroads of destiny has led us to? A pointlessly happy ending?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Eh, overthinking it would be equally pointless. Well, that's enough for one day — time to take a break.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could you be any more cryptic? You're planning something, Paimon knows it...

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Whatever happens, today was a breakthrough in my journey of discovery. I will go back and share it with my clan.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Me too.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: And me.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Let's leave it there for today then. I'm sure we'll find out what else Mr. Narrator has planned for us tomorrow.

talks.objective: Wait until after 08:00 the next day

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll be right back...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Sure. Don't worry, I'm not going anywhere!

dialogues.speaker: Bystander
dialogues.text: Oh my god, this is terrible! I don't understand, the three great clans of Constellation Metropole have finally made peace with each other. Who could have done this?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: What happened? Oh no, someone's lying on the ground... Cappet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did this happen?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Cappet, you idiot, wake up! You need to revise your last words, or everyone's gonna start suspecting me!

dialogues.speaker: Detective-Looking Dude
dialogues.text: Last words? What did he say?

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: "If I wind up dead one day, the murderer was Boborano."

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Gah, you could have at least pretended to not remember it!

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Boborano, but this is an interrogation. I have to give the detective straight answers...

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Boborano. I don't consider you a suspect, nor do I have the authority to charge anyone with a crime. So, are you the last people to have had contact with him?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Y—Yes...

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: My sincere condolences. You were travel companions, right? It's a real tragedy... I'm afraid he'll be out cold for another hour and a half, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: I know. It's despicable. Hitting someone in the back of the head is the second-worst act of cruelty there is. The first being replacing their gear oil with extra-strong glue.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: So... Cappet's... not dead?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: His gears, metal frame, and shell are all still in excellent condition. It's just his energy supply that's been all messed up...

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Wait, but... Surely you can't be suggesting that just because Cappet isn't broken, there's no need to go looking for the culprit...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No no, there's a need! Huge need.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: ...Unfortunately, this is rapidly turning into a cold case. There's no evidence, and no witnesses. Unless there's an official clockwork pedestal of the Goddess of Prophecy around here somewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: *cough* *cough* ...Ahem, excuse me.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Then, suddenly, the long-lost dragon of old flew across the sky!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Where, where?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: I didn't see anything... Wait, why can't I move?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: My mistake, it was just a cloud. Or a bird, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: If only we could turn time backwards and replay the crime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Isn't that one of those... clockwork socket things, right behind you?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: #Ah! So it is. No wonder everyone here is suddenly struggling to move. {NICKNAME}, if you please, let's recreate the crime scene.

talks.objective: Turn the clockwork base and rewind the truth

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: How could it be fake?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Well, that clears it up. Cappet was walking along the street, then he suddenly collapsed. He was faking it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What, so case closed? Aren't you supposed to investigate a little more first?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: We literally replayed the crime scene and saw it with our own eyes. There's no need for any evidence-gathering or powers of deduction now. Besides, maybe the truth is inherently strange by nature.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Like how Constellation Metropole has three histories, each of which is the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: But didn't you say Cappet was struck in the back of the head and knocked unconscious?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: For all I know, he could have bashed his head against the toilet bowl before leaving the house. Then walked here in a daze before finally passing out.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: As for why he might have done that... My guess is:

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: With the Supreme Clan question left unanswered, and the tension in Constellation Metropole suddenly wiped away, he was looking to create a new source of conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Only then would the city feel alive again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Do we really think he's capable of that, though? Sounds like a pretty complicated conspiracy for the average Simulanka resident...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, something about the crime scene isn't sitting right with me... It just seems unnatural.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Also, anything outside of the immediate area won't have appeared in the replay. Is it possible that something was missing from the scene?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Why don't we search the area?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Wait, what are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Oh, we're uh... we're gonna head to Cappet's house to check the toilet bowl for signs of an impact.

talks.objective: Search for suspicious places and clues

dialogues.speaker: Constellation Metropole Royal Guard
dialogues.text: Hello there. Have you seen my spear, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Constellation Metropole Royal Guard
dialogues.text: Someone was shouting about a dragon a minute ago, and I instinctively threw it into the sky, yeah...

talks.objective: Search for suspicious places and clues

dialogues.speaker: Shop Owner
dialogues.text: You're... not from these parts, are you? Just visiting?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Yep, that's right. Why, what's up?

dialogues.speaker: Shop Owner
dialogues.text: Ah. Well, I was gonna offer you a great job in the toytanium mines. A safe and secure working environment.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Uh... Doesn't sound very safe... At least, not as safe as being a courier.

dialogues.speaker: Shop Owner
dialogues.text: To keep the toytanium ore intact, we use specially designed pickaxes that can't cut through it. Even if you struck a person with it, it wouldn't so much as leave a scratch.

dialogues.speaker: Shop Owner
dialogues.text: And in terms of labor intensity, the work has been rated as class-two physical labor by a reputable organization. Even cats can do it.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I'm not a— Ugh, never mind. I give up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Welcome to Paimon's world...

dialogues.speaker: Shop Owner
dialogues.text: Mind you, I don't know what happened today, but somehow a pickaxe has gone missing. Maybe one of the giant guards broke down, so someone took it to perform a rapid resuscitation procedure.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Sounds pretty brutal for a first-aid technique...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: #Still, a missing pickaxe, huh... Is it just me, {NICKNAME}, or does that seem kinda suspicious?

talks.objective: Search for suspicious places and clues
Search for suspicious places and clues

dialogues.speaker: Grocery Store Owner
dialogues.text: *sigh* Come here — whatever it is you were looking to buy, please do come back tomorrow. It's just, I have to close early today.

dialogues.speaker: Grocery Store Owner
dialogues.text: A bottle of growth serum has gone missing. If someone's stolen it with the intention of harming others, the consequences could be disastrous.

dialogues.speaker: Grocery Store Owner
dialogues.text: There's a whole investigation into it, so I gotta close the shop while I do an inventory count. If it turns out I'm wrong and I miscounted, I could be charged with filing a false report and disturbing the peace...

talks.objective: Search for suspicious places and clues
Search for suspicious places and clues
Speak with Paimon and Kirara and deduce the murder weapon

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back. How was the toilet at Cappet's house?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Toilet? What about it? ...Oh yeah. Uh, forget that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Show the pickaxe)

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: What's this about? What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: We thought the way Cappet fell looked odd, so we searched the area for suspicious items and found this.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: It could have been deliberately placed out of range of the crime scene so it wouldn't show up when we replayed it. Now we've retrieved it, we were gonna replay it again — you don't mind, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... I just remembered, I forgot to turn off the clockwork switch in my kitchen, I think I'll just—

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Oh no, you stay right there!

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Uhh...

talks.objective: Put the pickaxe back at the scene
Turn the clockwork base and rewind the truth once more

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: ...So it was you.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Hehe, hahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: I would congratulate you for cracking the case, but since I did such an abysmal job of covering my tracks, you didn't exactly have your work cut out for you.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: So all I can say is:

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Catch me if you can!

dialogues.speaker: Constellation Metropole Royal Guard
dialogues.text: Why did my spear go...?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: That voice sounds familiar... Open the door!

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: My head's spinning. Albizzi just gave me a quick rundown of the situation. So you caught the detective?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorta, we chased him until he surrendered. Oh, and he asked us to pass on a message...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell the three about the rest of what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: ...And that they could have removed the great clockwork key if they'd just worked together.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Does he really think we didn't try that? 'Cause we did. After six months in that place.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: That was my bad. I thought it was a stupid idea at the time, so I didn't really exert myself.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: I, uh... I also sort of stopped trying after three years.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: You...! *sigh* Never mind, I'm partly to blame as well. On the second attempt, I just hugged the key and pretended like I was pulling as hard as I could.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: You guys are so lazy... My granny's neighbor's pet dog has nothing on you, and it spends all day every day sunbathing.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Anyway, you said you heard the voice of the Goddess of Fate at the end? That's amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: There is a world beyond our own after all.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: What would you guys say to taking a trip to the outside world some time? Otherwise, I got bashed in the back of the head for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Depends, do either of you know how to get there...? But yes, I agree, we should go. And not invite the detective, just to annoy him.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: But maybe the reason we never worried about whether we're real or not is that, unlike him, we weren't there to witness the creation of this world. We've never had any reason to doubt that we're real.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: If someone ever convinced me that these delightful dimwits, Cappet and Albizzi, weren't real... I'd be devastated.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: So, are you all set? Ready to start investigating?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Hey! Are you guys already finished with everything in the Metropole?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: No need to prioritize me — there's just this place I really wanna go check out. Feel free to get back to me once you've got everything sorted out.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The party finds no pedestal in which to place the great clockwork key, only a locked door.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Where's your clan's pedestal? Lemme guess, you hid it away in advance to save yourself the embarrassment of having it exposed as a fake?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: You done? Okay. Now, since my clan's main claim to fame is—

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Misinformation, half-truths, and fabrication...

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Oh, shut up, Cappet.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi & Narrator
dialogues.text: Shut up, Cappet.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: I swear, if I wind up dead one day, the murderer was Boborano. Let those be my last words.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: My clan's claim to fame is that we outwitted the dragon of old and stole its treasure. Ergo, all articles of value that we own — including the pedestal for the clockwork key — lie behind that door.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: So next step is, open the door?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Almost. There's one step before that. The door is protected by a smart interrogation system. We have to answer its questions, and if we get them wrong, it will alert law enforcement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez. Well, do you at least know the answers?

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: The correction fluid of time has dyed white the pages of the book of wisdom. ...Uh, no. No, I don't know the answers.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: But worry not, I had a quick word with the constabulary in advance. They'll ignore the alarm if we get the questions wrong. So answer without fear.

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (There is no response from the door, and nothing unusual about it.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Knock on the door.)

dialogues.speaker: Voice From Behind the Door
dialogues.text: Question 1: Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: You've got nowhere left to run!

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Alright, I confess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was fast!

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Getting caught by you here was a backup plan. I don't know if what I've done will make things better or not.

dialogues.speaker: Detective
dialogues.text: Time to come clean. I am the narrator, the one who's been guiding you all this time.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: Hahaha, okay. I guess my voice-acting skills have some room for improvement.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: Anyway, I only did what I did because—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why are you suddenly spilling the beans?

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: I poured my heart and soul into all this. I was worried you wouldn't ask.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: The truth is, I was one of the first conscious beings ever made by the Goddess of Creation. And I've known for a long time that this whole world is just a fairytale, written by the Goddess of Fate.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: I know they say that fairytales are just made up for kids to read. But I refuse to believe that fairytales are just fictional stories, and nothing more.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: The reason why Constellation Metropole has three origin stories is that the Goddess of Fate wrote three drafts, and couldn't decide which one she liked best.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: Then, her cat trod all over them and they all got crumpled together. So the three worlds just sort of folded into one.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: The Goddess of Fate was torn between them anyway, since she couldn't decide which ending was best for the dragon or the kids.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: So when she saw what the cat had done, she simply decided to go with all three.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who'd have thought... But what does any of this have to do with what you did?

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: You're not a fictional character, so you couldn't hope to understand my sorrow. Honestly, I don't think there's anyone in all of Simulanka who would understand.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: Every day that I experience, every interaction I have with another person... Is it really all just a work of fiction?

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: The only reason the three great clans wanted to find out the truth was for the pointless task of electing the Supreme Clan. I thought that once they'd learned the truth, it might make them curious enough to investigate further.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: But as it turned out, they just... accepted it. And carried on living the same old lives.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: I have to motivate them to keep looking for answers, now that they think they've learned the truth. I have to make them uncomfortable with the superficial explanation that they took at face value.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: And I have to figure out, once and for all, while you real people from the outside world are still here: Are we real?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw...

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: That's my full confession. Time for you to take me back. I'm guessing I'll probably be forced to make a public apology, then sentenced to half a day in solitary confinement. I definitely deserve half a day.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: Oh, also, pass this message onto Cappet, Boborano, and Albizzi, if you could: The great clockwork key was originally put in place jointly by the ancestors of the three clans.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: If the three of them had had any ability to cooperate whatsoever, they'd have been able to remove it by themselves.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: Over all these years, not once have they ever tried removing it together.
Oh, my poor child. There's one thing you've been mistaken about this whole time.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Aah! Whose voice is that!? ...Detective, was that you? Your voice acting's actually pretty good.
The reason fairytales are suitable for children is that they help them to understand the world.

Fairytales may be works of fiction, but at their heart lies an internal logic that is undoubtedly real-world truth in a condensed form. Perhaps they simplify good and evil, and perhaps they hide the darkness in metaphors.
But let there be no doubt: The world within fairytales is as real as can be. And by extension, you and your compatriots are also real.

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: Goddess! Is it really you!?

response.speaker: Footnote
response.text: The line that separates footnotes from narrative can never be crossed. Never the two shall meet. This is why you have never heard my voice before.

response.speaker: Footnote
response.text: But now, you wish to break free from the story — and there's a cat nearby — so you can hear my echo.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Nekomata...

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: ...Just your echo...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw... Poor detective...

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: So... we are a part of the real world, too...

response.speaker: Black Screen Text
response.text: You lead the surrendered detective back to Cappet...

response.speaker: Black Screen Text
response.text:
"So we need a shot of the crime scene for evidence, a mugshot of the suspect for the records, and a photo of the heroes for posterity..." The guard mulled it over. "Three photos is overkill. Let's just get one big group photo at the crime scene."

"Suspect, try and look more serious. Heroes, more natural please, happy smiles! ... But no smiling from the victim or their friends and family, thank you. No no, don't get up! Stay on the ground, we need to capture the crime-scene as-is!"


"3, 2, 1, say cheeeeese!"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Weirdest photo experience of my life...)

choices.text: Gasp! Shock! My mind is blown!

response.speaker: Detective
response.text: You're overdoing it a little bit there.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: I'm not hiding, I'm just looking for clues...

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: He's got no guts.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: I'm hiding...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Let's say one of these was the weapon used in the assault. Which one do you think it is?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The growth serum?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: If it was the growth serum, Cappet would've been turned into a giant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, the bottle probably would've shattered when it hit him. We would have seen the debris on the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Let's say one of these was the weapon used in the assault. Which one do you think it is?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The guard's spear?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: If so, there's no way his head would still be in such good shape. He'd have a big dent in the back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And if the guard is to be believed, he had the spear in his possession right up until that guy shouted about the dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Let's say one of these was the weapon used in the assault. Which one do you think it is?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The pickaxe?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If it was the pickaxe, Cappet sure is lucky it's not still lodged in his head...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Actually, you're wrong there, Paimon. The foreman at the mine was just saying, this kind of pickaxe is designed not to damage toytanium, so it couldn't cause any superficial damage to residents here.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: But, you could probably knock someone out if you hit them hard enough. And it wouldn't leave a scratch.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Let's take this back to the crime scene and replay it one more time.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I've delivered packages all over, but I've never seen a mysterious fairytale world like this before!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Nothing to see here, either... Maybe we can find someone to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Aha, over there! I bet we'll find some people there. Let's go take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: You wanna check out the area over there? Okay, I'll wait here for you.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Captivated by the epic poetry, and enthralled by the outstanding storytelling, the outlanders knew what their next objective was:

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Namely, to remove the <color=#00E1FFFF>clockwork key from the raised platform</color> up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Cappet, I just realized. You said we all had to speak like bards, but every time you open your mouth, I don't hear any rhymes.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Yeah, I noticed that too. It's one standard for us, and another for you. That's not fair, Cappet.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: We'll need the key again, right? Lemme see if I can pull it out... Yoink!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Guess I'll take the clockwork key again then? Yoink!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there really no way to get them to stop, Albizzi?

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Th—They'll receive new orders tomorrow, I assure you!

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: Actually, we already have what we need. Even if they catch us and throw us out, it's no great loss.

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Your wisdom is admirable, but that is not what a courageous person would do.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: I apologize. Empathy is not our giant guards' strong suit.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #"What a beautiful day!" Thought {NICKNAME}, before {M#he}{F#she} was overcome by a creeping sense of foreboding.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #The voice in {M#his}{F#her} head grew louder: "Must... go to... Pendulum Lane..."

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: That experience was, honestly, not the best. Reminds me of my childhood, when I had to walk along the tracks my parents had designed.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Back then, we even had to rotate on rack lines.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: I apologize. Empathy is not our giant guards' strong suit.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #"What a beautiful day!" Thought {NICKNAME}, before {M#he}{F#she} was overcome by a creeping sense of foreboding.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: #The voice in {M#his}{F#her} head grew louder: "Must... go to... Pendulum Lane..."

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: That experience was, honestly, not the best. Reminds me of my childhood, when I had to walk along the tracks my parents had designed.

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: Back then, we even had to rotate on rack lines.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I guess we should start here?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Hmm... Do we really need this one?

dialogues.speaker: Cappet
dialogues.text: Connect the lines to draw the family crest...

dialogues.speaker: Boborano
dialogues.text: This thing had better be the real deal...

dialogues.speaker: Albizzi
dialogues.text: This is so exciting...
